registry_note: Resolve the registry through npa.deploy.images / npa configure. Additive tags are pushed to both the primary (eu-north1) and mirror (us-central1) registries; never hardcode a registry id here.

target.rt_cores_note: Datacenter Blackwell has no RT cores, exactly like H100/H200. Rasterized rendering (Isaac Lab / SONIC isaac-render) must stay on L40S or RTX PRO 6000; only headless / state-based work routes here.
target.sass_compatibility: SASS is per-arch with no cross-major compatibility. sm_120 (major 12, RTX PRO 6000) binaries and sm_100/sm_103 (major 10) binaries are mutually incompatible, so validating on RTX PRO 6000 does not prove B200/B300. Within a major, minor-version forward compatibility holds: sm_100 SASS runs on sm_103, not the reverse. Build for sm_100 first and confirm on B300.
arch_knobs: Prebuilt torch wheels ship a fixed fat-binary arch set that TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST cannot change; only the wheel index does. cu128/cu130 include sm_100 and sm_120, cu124/cu126 stop at sm_90.

Source-compiled CUDA extensions (flash-attn from source, Taichi/Genesis, natten, custom ops) obey TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST. Omitting an arch yields 'no kernel image is available for execution on the device' at runtime.

verdicts.ready: The base wheel/toolchain already covers sm_100, so the image needs an additive rebuild plus live validation - no dependency changes.
verdicts.port: Needs a CUDA/torch bump or arch flags before it can target sm_100; the upstream wheels exist.
verdicts.blocked: Upstream does not ship the architecture yet. Track the upstream reason; never stub a fake pass.
verdicts.not-applicable: CPU-only or GPU-agnostic. It already runs on a B200/B300 host; only node-pool scheduling needs confirming.

validation_states.validated: get_device_capability() confirmed on a real B200/B300 node with the image's real capability smoke passing.
validation_states.pending-hardware: Wheel arch set confirmed on the built image, but not yet run on a real datacenter Blackwell node.
validation_states.not-required: CPU-only image; no arch assertion applies.

images.name: npa-base
images.smoke: gpu_capability_smoke.py: device capability + native SASS, bf16 matmul and torch SDPA as controls, then a flash-attn-4 CuTe forward pass checked against SDPA
images.notes: Gates most of the tree, so it is built and validated first. TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST was widened from 10.3 to cover both CUDA majors; the build asserts the wheel reports sm_80/sm_90/sm_100/sm_120. sm_103 is intentionally not asserted because stock cu130 wheels ship sm_100 SASS and B300 is reached by 10.0 -> 10.3 forward compat. The flash-attn-4 CuTe JIT was assumed to make this image usable on any Blackwell part; real-GPU testing disproved that for sm_120 - see known_gaps.flash_attn_sm120.

npa-base.wheel_arch_check: passed at image build time (the build asserts sm_80/sm_90/sm_100/sm_120)
npa-base.hardware_run: Run on two real GPU architectures by reusing already-deployed Kubernetes pools. On RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120): capability (12,0) confirmed, native SASS present, bf16 matmul and torch SDPA pass, and the checker correctly REFUSED a b200 target on that device (cross-major guard). On H100 (sm_90): the full capability smoke passes including the flash-attn-4 CuTe kernel, max abs error 0.00186 vs SDPA. Not yet run on B200 or B300 themselves.
npa-base.hardware_blocker: B200/B300 instances cannot be placed. Serverless jobs submit but their instance cycles STARTING -> STOPPED indefinitely, in both us-central1 (B200) and uk-south1 (B300); a VM deploy failed earlier still on the tenant's public IPv4 quota. The tenant's GPU quota has also read limit 2 / 2 in use for b200 and h200. This is shared capacity, not the image: the same image passes its full capability smoke on H100, and the same submission path fails identically on H200.
npa-base.how_to_finish: When a B200 or B300 node can be placed, run npa/scripts/blackwell-gpu-validation-job.yaml against it (or npa/scripts/validate_blackwell_image.sh <image> --target b200 --gpu), confirm capability (10,0) or (10,3) with the flash-attn kernel passing, and flip this entry's validation to 'validated'.

flash_attn_sm120.summary: flash-attn-4's CuTe forward kernel cannot execute on sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell). `import flash_attn` succeeds, so an import-only check reports a false pass.
flash_attn_sm120.error: AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute '_trait' in cutlass.cute.nvgpu.cpasync.tma_partition, reached from flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd.py epilogue via quack.copy_utils.tma_get_copy_fn
flash_attn_sm120.root_cause: The kernel partitions its epilogue with a TMA (Tensor Memory Accelerator) copy atom, and that atom is unavailable on workstation Blackwell. TMA is a datacenter feature: sm_90 (Hopper) and sm_100/sm_103 (datacenter Blackwell) have it, sm_120 does not.
flash_attn_sm120.evidence: Verified on a real NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition node (capability (12,0)). All four tested configurations (bf16/fp16, head_dim 64/128, seqlen 64/256) fail at the same line, so it is architecture-wide rather than config-specific. torch SDPA and a bf16 tensor-core matmul both succeed on the same device, ruling out the GPU and the wheel.
flash_attn_sm120.regression: No. The previously published npa-base:cuda13-b300-sm80-sm90-sm120-latest, built before the arch widen and the CUTLASS pin, fails identically on the same node. This is pre-existing and was hidden by an import-only golden eval.
flash_attn_sm120.does_not_affect: sm_100 and sm_103 have TMA, and the H100 control shows the kernel works wherever TMA exists, so datacenter Blackwell is expected to work. Still unverified on real B200/B300 silicon.
flash_attn_sm120.upstream_tracking: https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention - flash-attn-4 CuTe TMA path assumes a datacenter architecture
flash_attn_sm120.mitigation: gpu_capability_smoke.py --allow-no-tma records this as a known gap on non-TMA parts and still fails on datacenter parts, where a TMA failure would be real. Callers on sm_120 should use torch SDPA.
flash_attn_sm120.positive_control: The same image on a real NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 node (capability (9,0), which has TMA) runs flash_attn_func successfully with max abs error 0.00186 against torch SDPA. Same wheel, same flash-attn build, same CUTLASS pin - only the architecture differs. That isolates the cause to TMA availability and shows the kernel path itself is sound.
